note: Literature confirms that classic PCH subtypes (notably PCH2A) typically show normal prenatal and at-birth head circumference, with microcephaly and cerebellar anomalies often escaping prenatal sonography and manifesting postnatally.

evidence.text: In a homogeneous cohort of 33 patients with PCH2 carrying the TSEN54 p.A307S variant, weight, length, and head circumference were mostly in the normal range at birth and only later became severely microcephalic (-5.58 SD at age 5 years).

source.title: Natural course of pontocerebellar hypoplasia type 2A
source.quote: Weight, length and head circumference, mostly in the normal range at birth, became abnormal, especially head circumference (-5.58 SD at age 5 yrs).

numbers.metric: Mean head circumference SD at age 5 years

evidence.text: Detailed prenatal ultrasound imaging failed to reveal cerebellar dysgenesis in twins with TSEN54-associated PCH2, whose head circumferences crossed percentiles downward from the 50th centile at birth to below the 3rd centile by 6 months postnatally.

source.title: Molecular and neuroimaging findings in pontocerebellar hypoplasia type 2 (PCH2): is prenatal diagnosis possible?
source.quote: Head circumference curves for both twins crossed percentiles downward from 50th centile at birth to <3rd centile at 6 months
